written_before: the leaf was wired and before any whole-game differential was run with it
what: wiring the item-DISPOSITION leaf (`lastItem` / `ateBerry`) into engine/board_state.js

baseline.note: 0 of 961 with the leaf ABSENT. That zero is the number this prediction is against.

what_is_already_measured_and_therefore_n.removal_paths: 4 REMOVAL arms (Knock Off vs Leftovers, Knock Off vs Sitrus, Trick, Thief) read `-/--` on BOTH engines. The row's own `wrong_if` is FALSIFIED: no removal path in either engine writes either field. This is also what the source says — Showdown's `takeItem` (sim/pokemon.ts:1856-1870) writes neither, and Showdown has exactly THREE write sites in gen 9 (`eatItem` :1805 + :1809, `useItem` :1846; the `battle-actions.ts:128` carry is `gen <= 4`).
what_is_already_measured_and_therefore_n.berry_paths: 3 CONSUMPTION arms agree exactly: Colbur eaten inside the damage calculation, Sitrus eaten at `onUpdate`, and the same Sitrus record still on the BENCHED body after a switch. All read `<berry>/ate` on both engines.
what_is_already_measured_and_therefore_n.the_one_disagreement: `sash-used`. The authority writes `focussash / --` and medicham2 writes nothing at all. medicham2 has no `useItem` door: `_lastItem` is written ONLY in `consumeBerry`, so every non-berry SPEND goes unrecorded.

the_population_that_can_part.derived: every item in gen9championsvgc2026regmb whose consumption runs Showdown's `useItem` rather than `eatItem`
the_population_that_can_part.plus: Fling, whose own condition writes `lastItem`/`usedItemThisTurn` directly (data/moves.ts fling.condition.onUpdate) — medicham2's `_flingSpend` site writes neither

pool_prevalence_of_the_three_on_a_SHEET.caveat: THIS IS AN UPPER BOUND AND NOT THE PREDICTION. Carrying a Focus Sash is not spending one — the holder must be at full HP and take a lethal hit — and the differential brings only the first four buildable bodies per side.

stage_1_leaf_wired_engine_UNFIXED.board_material_of_961: NOT ZERO. Point estimate 250; stated interval 100 to 450.
stage_1_leaf_wired_engine_UNFIXED.why: the Sash is on 93.8% of pool sheets and a 50-turn empirical-click game gives it many chances to fire; every firing writes `lastItem` on the authority and nothing here, so the board parts on `active[].last_item` or `party.<body>.last_item` and stays parted for the rest of the game.
stage_1_leaf_wired_engine_UNFIXED.dominant_value: focussash on the authority against an empty string here
stage_1_leaf_wired_engine_UNFIXED.ate_berry_contribution: ZERO. Both engines route every berry through one consumption site and the probe shows three berry arms agreeing, including across a switch.
stage_1_leaf_wired_engine_UNFIXED.falsified_if: board-material comes back at or near 0. That would mean either the leaf is not reaching the comparison at all (an unwired knob gives identical output — CLAUDE.md) or the Sash never fires in this pool, and the FIRST of those must be excluded before the second is believed.

stage_2_leaf_wired_engine_FIXED.why: the fix records the spend at medicham2's four reachable non-berry consumption sites (White Herb in `restoreStatsUpdate`, Mental Herb in `mentalHerbCures`, the Focus Sash branch of `consumesItem`, and the Fling spend), which is the whole legal population above.
stage_2_leaf_wired_engine_FIXED.falsified_if: any residue remains — that would name a `useItem` path neither the source read nor the probe found.

second_order_effects_the_fix_carries.recycle: medicham2's Recycle is gated on `_lastItem` and could therefore only ever restore a berry. After the fix it restores a spent Sash or herb, which is what the authority does.
second_order_effects_the_fix_carries.harvest_belch_cudchew: UNAFFECTED — all three are gated on `_ateBerry`, which the fix does not set.

what_would_make_me_refuse_the_wire: a PARTS on a REMOVAL arm. There is none, so the wire proceeds.
note_on_the_artifact_row_that_asked_for_: `knock_off_roadmap_80.verdict` says *"Showdown records Colbur as EATEN BY ITSELF, medicham2 as KNOCKED OFF"*. That sentence is STALE. The same artifact's own `arms` block already shows both engines emitting `[eat]` then `[weaken]`, and the probe reads `colburberry/ate` on both. The predicted effect therefore does NOT come from Colbur; it comes from the Focus Sash, which that row does not mention.
